package: MATCH-V1: ONE shared "Odgovara mi" rule = kind of work + area + time. Four NEW private functions (worker_need_time_tier_v1, worker_need_fit_v1, worker_need_match_v1, requeue_changed_worker_profiles_v1), six REPLACED bodies (match_detail_without_calendar, dispatch_cheap_candidate_admitted, worker_dispatch_time_admitted, dispatch_next_wave, dispatch_tick, candidate_profile_ids) and two private.marketplace_config data rows (match_v1_profile_requeue = the watermark, match_v1_dispatch = the dispatch switch). Default dispatch mode ALL: one wave to every worker the rule admits, nearest first, up to a per-task-revision safety ceiling; the ladder 5/5/10/20 is kept behind the same row (mode LADDER). Tools, vehicles, experience and the minimum fee are no condition and no score. A direct profile write re-queues open tasks. No table, column, constraint, trigger, policy or grant on an existing object changed.

The ladder (switch-ladder-on.sql) is NOT switched on; it stays his word.

method.statement: candidate.in-transaction.sql sent byte-exact through the connector's apply_migration (the connector adds its own transaction and the ledger insert). The statement was sent byte-exact through the connector and the stored statement was read back from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations afterwards: 1 statement, 56949 characters (56950 bytes; one non-ASCII character, the z-caron in the notification title 'moze'), md5 0ec94359fbfb8015a78085535b13f114, equal to the md5 of the file.
method.insideTheStatement: Pre-guards in the same transaction: certificate ready; the four new functions and both new rows absent; the 16 dependency body md5 pins (the zone helper accepted in either of its two known states); the 6 predecessor body md5 pins. Each of the six replacements: preimage md5, md5 of the new body against the generator's value, exactly one anchor of the old body in pg_get_functiondef, then the whole pg_proc row apart from the body and the function comment asserted unchanged. Post-guards: the four new bodies pinned by md5 with security definer, volatility, owner postgres, search_path=pg_catalog and ACL {postgres=X/postgres}; the six replaced bodies pinned by md5; the 16 dependencies unchanged; the watermark row present; the dispatch row equal to the default; both closure digests equal before and after (a temporary table of the pre-apply digests) and the certificate ready. Any difference aborts and rolls back.

revert.effect: revert.sql restores the six predecessor bodies byte for byte and deletes the four new functions and both configuration rows, i.e. the ladder of before (refuses while DISCOVERY-ZAMENE is applied). Code and configuration rollback only: notifications and deliveries already written stay, and so does the ceiling change (the row is deleted).

notProven: No wave of the new rule has run on DEV data yet at the time of writing; the disposable-database proof (run 37662617758: zone, behaviour, load) covers the behaviour, the exact revert and the timing.
No HTTP/JWT test of a manual application (rpc_submit_response / rpc_select_response read responseAllowed) against DEV after the change.

The load numbers (300 and 1,000 matching workers, a tick of 25 tasks x 500 workers in about 24 s) come from a disposable server; a single wave to 10,000 workers was not measured (about 2 ms per worker, so about 20 s extrapolated) and 4 rows per notified worker are written. MATCH-V1B (waves for remote tasks) is the follow-up.
Push stays disabled: the PUSH notification rows of a wave are written but nothing is sent. No client change yet reads the new codes or the timeTier.

afterApplyConfig.why: the owner named a ceiling up to 10,000 notified workers per task revision; 10000 is the largest value the code accepts. The ceiling is a safety valve (four rows per notified worker), not a business rule.
afterApplyConfig.note: mode stays ALL; the ladder is not switched on. MATCH-V1B (remote tasks in waves) is the follow-up that makes a very large audience cheap; until it is applied a task with thousands of matching workers would be notified in one wave. DEV has 5 active worker profiles, so the ceiling cannot bind today.
